### Summary

All candidates proposed no modifications to the base harness. The harness code and prompt files remained constant across all four rollouts. The observed differences in outputs — base1 returned 91, inv1 returned 141, dom1 returned 85, agg1 returned 72 — reflect variation in the LLM model's own computation or behavior on repeated invocations of the identical harness, not a response to any control-flow change or structural improvement. The decision notes correctly identify this as expected stochasticity. The adoption of agg1 was not driven by superior harness engineering: the selection reason explicitly notes "trivial pool: single final at k=1; delivered without a selector session," indicating agg1 was chosen as the only candidate presented for delivery, not selected competitively. With zero harness edits across the pool, no execution contrast attributable to changes in code or configuration exists to establish a transferable lesson.
